summary: First verification of milestone M1 (Enterprise and Renewal data model) in build northwind-sales. Both steps are documented, no step is blocked, and the plan gate is approved, so the precondition holds and M1 has no predecessor milestone. Verdict ready-with-findings: 28 cross-step references resolved with 0 unresolved and 0 unclassifiable; deployment order agrees with every artefact's type and no dependency runs backwards; the merged manifest (5 types, 9 members, one version 62.0, no member collision) is byte-identical to the manifest the org validated on mock-deploy run 4; both runnable declared acceptance tests exit as expected and the two manual ones are collected into a six-line gate checklist. It is not ready-for-gate because three things a reader of that word would not expect are true: the OpportunityStage value set is a fragment that deactivates the SMB pipeline if deployed as it stands (O-M1S01-01, A24 high), requirement item 2's Opportunity Products related list has no artefact and no test (REQ-010, an ERROR from check_rtm.py), and which stage a new Opportunity opens on is UNVERIFIED (O-M1S01-04). Eight open items carried; approving the gate accepts all eight. The three checker-coverage WARNs were run as undeclared advisory evidence and two of the three assert nothing at all over M1's artefacts.
confidence_rationale: Every MEDIUM/LOW trigger in the agent's own Step 10 table is absent and every HIGH condition is met on a literal reading, but reaching HIGH needs two interpretive stretches, so the score is held one step down. (1) The HIGH row requires 'every declared acceptance test ran'; two of M1's four declared tests are `manual` and were collected rather than run, and the playbook's 'every runnable test' carve-out is written for scale: ask only and does not extend to this scale: project plan. (2) The Step 3 trichotomy (resolved here / resolved earlier / unresolved) has no outcome for the 12 standard-field layout references, which no symbol inventory could hold and which rest on org evidence from a mock-deploy run this agent did not perform. Nothing about the verification's coverage is in doubt: the artefact set was complete, all 13 recorded artefact hashes matched on disk, and the resolution, order, merge and manifest checks were computed rather than asserted.

They rest on org evidence (mock-deploy run 4, checkOnly, 9/9 Succeeded) that this agent read rather than produced.
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Nothing to retry in-build; standard-field references are only ever settled by a validation against the org, which run 4 already provides.

The other two are type `manual` and are collected into the Step 7 checklist rather than run — by the playbook's own instruction that manual tests go to Step 7, and because no agent may tick a manual test on a human's behalf.

findings.title: REQ-010: requirement item 2's Opportunity Products related list has no artefact and no test
findings.detail: Neither layout ships a relatedLists block, so a rep who opens either page as deployed cannot add a product line. requirement.md item 2 ('reps add products from our price book to every Enterprise opportunity') is not satisfied by milestone M1. check_rtm.py, run this session exactly as traceability.md documents, reports ERROR row 11: coverage gap: REQ-010 has no test id while status is 'In Build'. This verifier confirmed independently that the gap is uncatchable by any test M1 declares: a grep for 'relatedList' across check_record_type_layouts.py, check_opportunity_management.py and check_products_and_pricebooks.py returns nothing, so no checker cited anywhere in M1 reads for the element.

evidence.linter_result: 10 rows, build schema, 1 coverage gap, 0 orphans, 1 error, 14 warnings

findings.recommendation: Close it one of two ways at the gate, never by re-labelling the status: (a) the O-M1S02-01 retrieve produces a relatedLists block in both layouts AND a test that reads for one, or (b) a human re-homes requirement item 2 onto a later step. The related-list API name is a retrieval alias present in no skill in this library and must be copied verbatim from a live-org retrieve, not typed.

findings.title: BLOCKING before any real deploy: the shipped OpportunityStage value set is a fragment, not a deployable file
findings.detail: standardValueSets/OpportunityStage.standardValueSet-meta.xml contains only the eight new Northwind stages. For a value set, omission is the deactivate instruction: deploying it as it stands deactivates every OpportunityStage value it does not name, including every stage the SMB team's generic pipeline runs on — which is precisely the requirement (requirement.md item 6) this milestone was told not to break. No validation can surface this: mock-deploy run 1 records the partial value set validating cleanly, because a checkOnly deploy never deactivates anything. A green dry run is not evidence here.
findings.recommendation: Gate checklist lines 1 and 5 are the same fact at two altitudes — line 1 confirms the instruction is written down, line 5 requires a named owner to own having done it. The merge is sf project retrieve start --metadata "StandardValueSet:OpportunityStage", keeping the org's existing <default>true</default> untouched and retiring values with <isActive>false</isActive> rather than deleting the element.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED: which stage a new Enterprise or Renewal Opportunity opens on
findings.detail: After the N3-F-01 repair removed <default>true</default> from both business processes (the org rejects a default on an Opportunity BusinessProcess outright), none of M1-S01's five cited skills documents a per-BusinessProcess or per-RecordType default-stage mechanism for Opportunity. The likely mechanism is that the Stage field takes whatever stage carries <default>true</default> on the global value set with no per-process override, but no cited skill states this for Opportunity, and if the org's existing global default is not a member of the Enterprise or Renewal stage subset the answer is unresolved by anything in this step's skills.

evidence.section: § 6, 'Where the default stage now comes from'

findings.recommendation: Closed only by the post-deploy SOQL in deploy-order.md § 4, cross-checked against each process's stage subset — never by reading what the UI shows as selected by default.

findings.title: MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 4 states the CloseDate inference as confirmed; run 4 proves sufficiency, not necessity
findings.detail: CloseDate carries behavior=Required on both layouts on the strength of an inference (Opportunity's three nillable=false standard fields are Name, StageName, CloseDate), set in the same repair pass as StageName, one round ahead of any deploy message naming it. Run 4 then validated the pair 9/9. That proves the shipped configuration deploys; it cannot distinguish 'the platform requires CloseDate on the layout' from 'Required is merely accepted there', because no run ever tested CloseDate at Edit after the other three were fixed, and run 3's silence proves nothing under the one-field-per-run behaviour. reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 4 nonetheless says the UNVERIFIED marker 'resolves to confirmed at the next doc-keeper pass' and its closing line counts CloseDate among four org facts. That reading goes one step past the evidence, and it sits in the document a gate reader is most likely to skim. Three fields are org-confirmed: Probability, Name, StageName. This report does not state CloseDate as an org fact.
findings.recommendation: The close condition is cheap and decisive and was not run here: one further scripts/mock_deploy.py round against a copy of either layout with CloseDate back at behavior=Edit and everything else unchanged. It matters beyond this build — the fact is on its way into the library, and a skill rule asserting CloseDate is layout-required on Opportunity would claim more than this evidence carries. A rule saying the four-item set validates is exactly what was observed.

findings.title: Two of the three checker-coverage WARNs name a checker that can assert nothing over M1's artefacts, and a third passes a broken value set at the scope it was run
findings.detail: The three § 5 WARNs on M1 could not be declared (amend-step refuses a step past pending/blocked, and both are documented), so all three checkers were run as undeclared advisory evidence at --manifest-dir artefacts. All three exit 0, and the exit codes are close to meaningless. check_opportunity_management.py says so itself ('Nothing in this tree is in scope for this checker') — it reads fixed paths at depth 1 with glob, not rglob; the declared M1-S01 step test already runs it at artefacts/M1-S01 where it does assert. check_products_and_pricebooks.py scans classes/, triggers/, settings/, flows/, profiles/, objects/Product2 and objects/PricebookEntry, none of which exist in M1 — structurally vacuous, so no invocation against M1 could assert anything. check_sales_process_mapping.py looks the most convincing and is the most misleading: its stage-metadata check reads one fixed path, <manifest-dir>/standardValueSets/OpportunityStage.standardValueSet-meta.xml, and the file is one level deeper. Confirmed by negative control in the session scratchpad (nothing in the build directory was touched): a copy of the tree with an illegal <forecastCategory>Commit</forecastCategory> and a wrong probability injected still exits 0 with 'No issues found.' at --manifest-dir artefacts, and exits 1 naming the enum violation at --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S01.

evidence.negative_control: broken tree: build scope exit 0 'No issues found.'; step scope exit 1 'ERROR: Stage Propose: <forecastCategory>Commit</forecastCategory> is not a member of the ForecastCategories enumeration'

findings.recommendation: At the next documented → running rebuild of M1-S01, declare admin/sales-process-mapping's checker at --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S01 (via amend-step --add-checker), not at tree root — that is the only scope at which its exit code carries an assertion. Do not quote any of the three build-scope exit codes in this run as evidence.

findings.title: Design question unresolved at the gate: the Enterprise and Renewal layouts are byte-identical
findings.detail: Both layout files hash to 0ee76271ffc8d988f8d7d18369e1be1f — byte-for-byte identical, differing only in file name, and confirmed still identical after all three of the 2026-09-18 org-driven repairs (every org message named both files, never one alone). The declared milestone checker surfaces this as its REVIEW finding. Nothing in Q14, Q20 or the step's inputs gives the Renewal motion a field the Enterprise motion does not also carry; the second file exists because decision D2 produced two record types.
findings.recommendation: A human decides at this gate: keep two files (defensible — it leaves room for the motions to diverge without a later record-type change) or merge to one shared layout. Recorded as a question because inventing a Renewal-specific field or collapsing the pair would each assert an answer nobody gave.
